source: 27-agent adversarial workflow wf_b703ac64-269 (map 6 dimensions -> 2-lens verify -> critic); 36 confirmed + 5 critic adds, 2 refuted

confirmed.title: Systemic: no code path anywhere distinguishes 'at the real limit' from any other permission-denied — the limit toast is a blind guess
confirmed.where: src/utils/errors.js:16-22; src/api/firebase-database.js (every catch returns only {error: error.message, code: error.code}); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:457,493-495,583-584
confirmed.scenario: Any Firestore-rules denial OR rules-evaluation error (missing parent doc null-value error, validity failure, auth lapse, malformed config/app.plans) returns code 'permission-denied'; apiErrorMessage maps that code unconditionally to limitMsg. The ONLY limit detection in the app is the client-side pre-checks against LOCAL React state (portfolios.length>=maxPortfolios at 457, portfolio.length>=lim at 493-495, currentTxCount>=maxTxPerCoin at 583-584) — and those are bypassed in exactly the scenarios that diverge local state from the DB (stale activePortId='default', trimToTier local-only trim per confirmed fact 5, client tier > DB tier). So the server-denial path can NEVER be honest: after a write fails there is zero verification that a limit was actually hit.
confirmed.fixIdea: Two-layer fix. (a) Data layer: before/after a denied addCoin, getDoc the parent portfolio — if it doesn't exist return code 'not-found' (distinct message: 'That portfolio no longer exists'); optionally inspect error.message for 'Null value'/'evaluation error' to classify rules-eval errors separately from clean denials. (b) UI layer: only show limitMsg when a fresh server read confirms count >= limit (re-read portfolio.coinCount + users.tier from server on permission-denied); otherwise show a neutral 'Couldn't save — please refresh and try again.' Also console.error(res.error) at every site so diagnostics stop being silently discarded.

confirmed.title: addCoin (the founder's bug site): five distinct non-limit failures all surface as 'You've reached this portfolio's coin limit — upgrade for more.'
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:498; src/api/firebase-database.js:171-190; firestore.rules:170-174,259-265,269-278,284-290
confirmed.scenario: Starter user with 2 coins adds a coin → toast claims the coin limit is reached. Non-limit permission-denied causes at this site: (1) activePortId names a nonexistent portfolio (initial 'default' from usePortfolios.js:14, or an id deleted on another device) → rules get() on missing parent → Null value error → denied [CONFIRMED fact 3 — the actual founder-bug mechanism]; (2) coin name >64 chars from the search API → validCoinData fails [CONFIRMED fact 4]; (3) invalid journal: priceAtAdd null [CONFIRMED fact 4], thesis/changeMyMind >2000 chars (Search.jsx textareas have NO maxLength — grep confirms the only maxLength in src/ is the rename input at CryptoIdea.jsx:847), or a funnel field >2000 chars (cleanFunnel in src/utils/journal.js:8-16 trims but never caps length) → validJournal/validFunnel fail; (4) auth token lapse/sign-out mid-write → isOwner fails; (5) users/{uid} doc missing (admin hard-delete while signed in) → tierOf() null-value eval error. In every case the user is told to pay for an upgrade that will not fix anything.
confirmed.fixIdea: Per the systemic fix, plus targeted pre-write validation: clamp/validate coin name <=64 and thesis/changeMyMind/funnel fields <=2000 client-side with specific messages (mirror the R10-2b pattern that already fixed negative amounts at CryptoIdea.jsx:575-581); have addCoin verify the target portfolio exists (or validate activePortId against the loaded portfolios list before writing) and return 'not-found' distinctly.

confirmed.title: Transaction EDIT passes the tx-limit upgrade message at a site where a real limit is structurally impossible
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:607; src/api/firebase-database.js:307-322; firestore.rules:196,305-317
confirmed.scenario: User edits an existing transaction and types an amount over 1e15 (plausible for quadrillion-supply meme tokens) or a price over 1e9, or their auth token has lapsed → updateDoc denied → toast: 'You've reached this coin's transaction limit — upgrade for more.' But the tx-update rule (firestore.rules:196) is only `validTransactionData() || isAdmin` — it touches NO counter and NO limit; editing an existing tx cannot hit any plan limit under any circumstances. Every permission-denied at this site is by definition a non-limit failure, yet the site unconditionally labels it a limit and solicits an upgrade. The client pre-check (CryptoIdea.jsx:579-581) validates only _amt>0/_prc>0, not the rules' upper bounds (amount<=1000000000000000, priceAtBuy<=1000000000 at rules:310,313).
confirmed.fixIdea: Remove the limitMsg argument from the line-607 call (the edit path) — the generic fallback is more honest — and add client-side upper-bound checks mirroring rules:310/313 with specific messages ('Amount too large — max 1,000,000,000,000,000').

confirmed.title: createPortfolio: a >50-char portfolio name (no client cap on the ADD inputs) is reported as 'You've reached your plan's portfolio limit — upgrade for more.'
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:456-461; src/components/Account.jsx:286; src/components/PortfolioBar.jsx:40; firestore.rules:150-154,252-257
confirmed.scenario: User types a 51+ char portfolio name in the Account or PortfolioBar add field (neither input has maxLength — the only maxLength in src/ is the RENAME input at CryptoIdea.jsx:847, and only renamePortfolio checks length at line 484; addPortfolio at 458 checks only non-empty) → validPortfolioData fails (rules:256 name.size()<=50) → permission-denied → the portfolio-limit upgrade toast. Also reachable via: users/{uid} doc missing → tierOf() null-value eval error; auth lapse; malformed config/app.plans (rules:71-72 .get chain eval error). Note the real-limit case DOES exist at this site (post-increment portfolioCount > maxPortfolios, e.g. the documented client-tier>DB-tier ERRORS.md §A1 case), so the limitMsg is sometimes honest — but nothing separates the honest case from the four dishonest ones.
confirmed.fixIdea: Add maxLength={50} to both add-portfolio inputs and mirror the rename check `if(name.length>50)` in addPortfolio before the write.

confirmed.title: addTransaction: missing/stale coin doc, out-of-bounds values, and legacy-invalid coin docs all surface as the tx-limit upgrade toast
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:614; src/api/firebase-database.js:285-304; firestore.rules:179,191-194,305-317
confirmed.scenario: (1) Coin removed on a second device while sel is stale → the batch's txCount bump targets a missing coin doc and the create rule's get(coinRef) hits a missing doc → null-value eval error → permission-denied → 'You've reached this coin's transaction limit — upgrade for more.' (fact-3 mechanism, one level down). (2) amount>1e15 or priceAtBuy>1e9 (client checks only >0) → validTransactionData fails → same toast. (3) The counter bump on the coin doc must pass validCoinData+counterDeltaOk on the MERGED doc (rules:179) — a coin doc with any legacy-invalid field (e.g. pre-validation journal shape) makes every future tx add fail with the limit toast. (4) Auth lapse / users-doc-missing (maxTx→tierOf eval error) → same toast. The real tx limit is also reachable here when local entries are stale vs DB txCount (trimToTier never deletes docs, fact 5), making the pre-check at 583-584 pass while the server correctly denies.
confirmed.fixIdea: Same as the systemic fix; additionally addTransaction could return 'not-found' when the coin doc doesn't exist (one getDoc on failure), and the client should validate the rules' upper bounds.

confirmed.title: Seven no-limit operations (delete portfolio/coin/tx, rename, thesis review/save/edit/delete) default to '...you may have reached a plan limit.' on every permission-denied
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:469,488,508,520,535,549,558,563,627; src/utils/errors.js:19
confirmed.scenario: None of these operations is gated by any limit rule — deletes and renames and journal updates touch no maxPortfolios/maxCoins/maxTx check in firestore.rules (delete: rules:160,181,198 are bare isOwner; rename: rules:157 validity+counter only; journal: rules:179 validity+counter only). Yet apiErrorMessage's no-limitMsg default is 'That action isn't allowed — you may have reached a plan limit.' Concrete triggers: (a) remCoin (563) with a stale activePortId → the coinCount decrement targets a missing portfolio doc → counterDeltaOk reads resource.data on null → eval error → permission-denied → the user is told a plan limit may block them from DELETING a coin (an operation that frees capacity); (b) deleteTransaction (627) with the parent coin gone → same mechanism on the coin doc; (c) reviewThesis/saveFunnel/addThesis/editThesis (508/520/535/549) on a coin deleted on another device, or with >2000-char thesis/funnel text (no client caps, see finding 2) → validJournal/validFunnel fail → 'may have reached a plan limit' for saving a note; (d) renamePortfolio (488) on a concurrently-deleted portfolio; (e) auth lapse at any of the seven. Suggesting an upgrade for operations where limits cannot apply is the same dishonesty class as the founder's bug, hedged.
confirmed.fixIdea: Change the apiErrorMessage default for permission-denied to a limit-neutral message ('That action isn't allowed — try refreshing, or sign in again.') and pass limitMsg ONLY at the three create sites (461, 498, 614) where a limit denial is actually possible.

confirmed.title: 'Check your connection.' fallback mislabels not-found: editing a transaction deleted on another device blames the network
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:607 (fallback arg); src/api/firebase-database.js:307-322; firestore.rules:196
confirmed.scenario: Device B deletes a transaction; device A still shows it and the user edits it → updateDoc on the missing tx doc. Uniquely among these writes, the tx-update rule references only request.resource.data (never resource), so rules PASS and Firestore returns NOT_FOUND → code 'not-found' → apiErrorMessage falls through to 'Couldn't save transaction. Check your connection.' — the connection is fine; the record is gone. (Most other missing-doc writes in this app instead become permission-denied via resource null-value eval errors and hit the limit-message findings above; this is the one site where missing-doc reliably yields 'not-found', and it's mislabeled too.)
confirmed.fixIdea: Add a 'not-found' branch to apiErrorMessage ('That item no longer exists — it may have been deleted on another device. Refresh to sync.') and have callers refresh local state on it.

confirmed.title: C-A3 metas watcher removes a remotely-deleted active portfolio but never repairs activePortId — every write then targets a ghost id and shows the limit toast
confirmed.where: src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:88-94 (watchPortfolios callback calls only setPortfolios, never setActivePortId); src/hooks/usePortfolios.js:15 (dangling id silently derives portfolio=[]); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:497 (addCoin writes to activePortId); firestore.rules:170-174 (get() on the missing parent -> Null value -> permission-denied)
confirmed.scenario: Pro user with p1+p2, active p2 on device A. On device B (or another tab) they delete p2. Device A's watchPortfolios snapshot rebuilds portfolios=[p1] but activePortId stays "p2". UI looks like a normal EMPTY portfolio (find-or-[] fallback); if the user is/becomes free-tier the PortfolioBar hides entirely (PortfolioBar.jsx:19) so there is no way to switch to p1. Every addCoin/addEntry/reviewThesis/remCoin now targets users/{uid}/portfolios/p2 which no longer exists -> rules get() Null-value -> permission-denied -> "You've reached this portfolio's coin limit — upgrade for more." Persists until logout/reload (and even reload only heals via the savedActive guard).
confirmed.fixIdea: Add a single invariant effect (e.g. in CryptoIdea.jsx or usePortfolios): whenever portfolios changes and !portfolios.find(p=>p.id===activePortId), setActivePortId(portfolios[0]?.id). This one guard also fixes the trim and load-failure dangles below.

confirmed.title: Registration step-2 failure (or any account with zero portfolio docs) leaves a permanent phantom "default" portfolio — UI looks normal but every addCoin fails with the limit toast, with NO recovery path
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-auth.js:93-104 (default-portfolio batch is a separate, failable second write; comment claims 'recoverable on next load'); src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:36-41 (loadPortfolios: `if (ports.length > 0)` — zero ports leaves state = DEFAULT_PORTFOLIOS + activePortId "default"); src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:89 (`if (!metas.length) return` — the watcher also never fixes the empty case); src/hooks/usePortfolios.js:4,13-14
confirmed.scenario: User registers; the network blips between the profile setDoc and the default-portfolio batch (or the tab closes). users/{uid} exists with portfolioCount 0 and no portfolio docs. On every subsequent login loadPortfolios succeeds with 0 portfolios, so portfolios stays the DEFAULT_PORTFOLIOS mock ({id:"default", name:"My Portfolio", coins:[]}) and activePortId stays "default". The Portfolio tab looks completely normal (empty "My Portfolio"). Every addCoin targets users/{uid}/portfolios/default, which does not exist -> Null-value rules error -> permission-denied -> the coin-limit toast, forever. Nothing in the codebase ever re-creates the default portfolio; the registration comment's 'recoverable on next load' is false. (Only accidental escape: manually creating a new portfolio via Account/addPortfolio.)
confirmed.fixIdea: In loadPortfolios, when getPortfolios succeeds with 0 portfolios for a signed-in user, self-heal: call createPortfolio(uid,"My Portfolio",0) (rules allow it — portfolioCount is 0) and use its real id; never leave the mock "default" as a write target.

confirmed.title: Forced sign-out paths never reset portfolios/activePortId/ci-active-port — next login on the same device can show the PREVIOUS account's coins (phantom holdings + privacy leak) and write to the previous account's portfolio id
confirmed.where: src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:99-102 (fbUser==null branch: only setUser(null)+setScreen — no setPortfolios/setActivePortId reset); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:386-394 (signOutEverywhere: also no portfolio-state reset and no db.del("ci-active-port")); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:253-260 (the cleanup lives ONLY in logout()); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:158-161 (ci-active-port key is global, not uid-keyed)
confirmed.scenario: User A (2 coins in p1) is signed out WITHOUT the logout button — token revoked by 'Sign out everywhere' from another device, a password change, adminSignOutUser, or the in-app signOutEverywhere handler. portfolios still holds A's coins and activePortId=A's portfolio id at the login screen. User B now logs in on the same device and B's loadPortfolios fails or returns zero portfolios (findings 2/3): B sees A's portfolio WITH A's coins (phantom data + a shared-device privacy leak), and addCoin writes under B's uid to A's portfolio id -> missing parent -> the limit toast. Even when B's load succeeds, the window between login and load renders A's stale state.
confirmed.fixIdea: Do the reset in useAuthSession's fbUser==null branch (setPortfolios(DEFAULT_PORTFOLIOS); setActivePortId("default")) so EVERY sign-out path is clean, and key the saved id per user: "ci-active-port-"+uid.

confirmed.title: Downgrade trimToTier drops the active portfolio from LOCAL state only — activePortId dangles against local state while the portfolio still exists server-side, so addCoin SILENTLY SUCCEEDS into an invisible portfolio
confirmed.where: src/hooks/useUpgrade.js:39-48,108-112 (trimPortfolios slice(0,lim.ports), never touches activePortId, never deletes server docs — empirical fact #5); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:660-682 (checkSubscriptionStatus calls trimToTier at load, after activePortId was restored to the saved id); src/components/PortfolioBar.jsx:19 (bar hides for a free 1-portfolio user — no manual escape)
confirmed.scenario: Pro user with p1+p2, last-active p2 (saved in ci-active-port). Subscription lapses; at next login loadPortfolios restores activePortId="p2", then checkSubscriptionStatus -> trimToTier("free") -> local portfolios=[p1] but activePortId stays "p2". UI: empty portfolio, PortfolioBar hidden (now free/1-portfolio). addCoin writes to p2 — which STILL EXISTS on the server with 4 coins (< free cap 10) — the write SUCCEEDS, but setPortfolio maps over local ids and no-ops: the coin appears NOWHERE, no error, no toast. Alternatively any tx/journal write also lands in the invisible portfolio. Bonus inconsistency: the next watchPortfolios metas snapshot rebuilds [p1,p2] from the server, silently UNDOING the trim — the trim is cosmetic and timing-dependent.
confirmed.fixIdea: After trimToTier, clamp activePortId to the kept set (the finding-1 invariant covers it). Longer-term: reconcile the trim server-side (delete over-limit docs via a callable) or stop trimming locally and gate by activePortId position instead — the metas watcher makes a local-only trim incoherent.

confirmed.title: logout()'s ci-active-port cleanup is immediately undone by the persistence effect — the C-R2a shared-device cleanup never actually happens
confirmed.where: src/CryptoIdea.jsx:258-260 (db.del("ci-active-port") then setActivePortId("default")); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:158-161 (effect [activePortId,dataLoaded] re-writes the key after the logout render; dataLoaded is never reset to false)
confirmed.scenario: User logs out. db.del removes ci-active-port, but setActivePortId("default") triggers the persistence effect (dataLoaded is still true), which writes ci-active-port="default" right back to localStorage. Functionally benign today only because loadPortfolios validates the saved id (useAuthSession.js:40), but the intended C-R2a 'clear this device's cached local data' is defeated, and any future code that trusts the saved id without the find-guard inherits a cross-account dangling id.
confirmed.fixIdea: Uid-key the storage key ("ci-active-port-"+uid) so the write after logout is harmless, or skip persisting when user is null.

confirmed.title: getPortfolios failure at login leaves activePortId="default" while the metas watcher later repairs only the ARRAY — split-brain for any user whose real portfolio id isn't "default" (all seeded users; any user whose original default was ever deleted)
confirmed.where: src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:29-30 (`if (!res.success) return;` — no retry, activePortId never set); src/api/firebase-database.js:65-75 (getPortfolios has NO auth-lag retry, unlike getUserProfile's documented retry at firebase-database.js:50-55); src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:88-94 (initial watchPortfolios snapshot then replaces portfolios with real metas, coins:[] — but never sets activePortId)
confirmed.scenario: Right after sign-in the Firestore client's auth state can lag and the first read throws permission-denied (the code documents this exact failure for getUserProfile and retries there — but not for getPortfolios). loadPortfolios early-returns; activePortId stays "default", portfolios stays the mock. Moments later the watchPortfolios initial snapshot delivers the real metas ([p1]) and replaces the array — now portfolios=[p1 (coins shown empty)], activePortId="default" (dangling). Seeded user admin@test.com: UI shows an empty-looking normal portfolio while p1 with 2 coins exists server-side; addCoin targets "default" -> missing parent -> the limit toast. For registration-created accounts the id happens to literally be "default" so it self-heals — but any account whose portfolios were created via addPortfolio (auto ids, e.g. after deleting/recreating) dangles in production too.
confirmed.fixIdea: Give getPortfolios the same transient-error retry as getUserProfile; and add the invariant-repair effect from finding 1 so a later metas snapshot fixes activePortId too.

confirmed.title: deletePortfolio on a stale/phantom entry silently corrupts portfolioCount (rules allow deleting a nonexistent doc + unconditional -1), and two stale devices can leave an account with ZERO portfolios
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-database.js:98-122 (batch always decrements portfolioCount, no existence check); firestore.rules:160 (allow delete: isOwner — no resource-exists or last-portfolio guard); firestore.rules:127-132 (counterDeltaOk permits the ±1 regardless); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:465-471 (client guard `portfolios.length<=1` runs on possibly-stale local state; `||"default"` fallback would itself set a ghost id)
confirmed.scenario: (a) Double delete: device A deletes p2; before device B's metas snapshot lands, B's Account list still shows p2 and the user taps Remove — the delete of the already-missing doc passes rules (nothing reads resource) and portfolioCount decrements a SECOND time, drifting below the real count (even negative). The portfolio-cap rule (getAfter==get+1 && <=max) now permanently miscounts — a free user gains an extra slot. (b) Zero-portfolio account: user has p1+p2 on two stale devices; A deletes p1 (guard sees 2), B deletes p2 (guard still sees 2) -> server has ZERO portfolios. Every future login then enters finding 2's unrecoverable phantom-"default" state: normal-looking empty UI + the limit toast on every addCoin. The 'need at least 1 portfolio' guarantee is client-side per-device only.
confirmed.fixIdea: Run the delete in a transaction that first reads the portfolio doc and aborts if missing; add `resource != null` semantics by ruling `allow delete: if isOwner(userId) && exists(...)` is implicit — instead enforce the floor server-side (deny delete when get(userRef).data.portfolioCount <= 1) and skip the counter decrement when the doc was already gone.

confirmed.title: Re-adding a coin the server already has inflates coinCount forever (the reported false-limit toast)
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-database.js:171-186 (addCoin: batch.set + increment(1)); client stale-list guard src/CryptoIdea.jsx:493; firestore.rules coin-update L179 + portfolio-update L157
confirmed.scenario: A coin exists on the server but is missing from the client's local `portfolio` array — reachable when (a) it was added on another device and watchCoins (active-portfolio-only, has a load window) hasn't synced yet, (b) the initial getCoins load hasn't populated `portfolio` yet, or (c) a fast double-tap on Add fires before the optimistic setPortfolio runs. The `portfolio.find(...)` "Already added" guard (and Search's disabled +Add, which reads the same array) fail OPEN. addCoin then runs batch.set on the EXISTING coin doc — Firestore evaluates this under the coin UPDATE rule (L179), which passes when the existing txCount is 0 or 1 (counterDeltaOk) — together with increment(coinCount, +1). No new coin doc is created, yet coinCount rises by 1 and NEVER self-heals (no reconciler anywhere). Once coinCount exceeds the real count, the server coin-CREATE rule (getAfter(coinCount) <= maxCoins, L174) denies the next genuine add while the client still shows room, and apiErrorMessage maps permission-denied to the exact reported toast "You've reached this portfolio's coin limit — upgrade for more." (CryptoIdea.jsx:498). EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED on the live emulator: addCoin returned success, coinCount 1->2 with real coins=1; the overwrite also reset the coin's txCount 1->0 (tx doc still present) and drops any existing `journal` (addCoin only writes journal when a new one is passed).
confirmed.fixIdea: Make addCoin refuse when the coin doc already exists so a re-add can never bump coinCount: either read the coin doc first and no-op/return an "already added" result, or write with a create-only guard (setDoc without overwrite / a batch whose success implies a real create). Ideally also tighten the coin rule so a `set` that leaves coinCount unchanged is the only allowed update path, so a stale client can't inflate the counter. Separately, wiping journal/txCount on overwrite is data loss even when it "succeeds."

confirmed.title: removeCoin decrements coinCount unconditionally, so a stale/duplicate delete drives coinCount below the real count (even negative)
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-database.js:259-273 (removeCoin: batch.delete + increment(coinCount,-1), no existence guard); firestore.rules portfolio-update L157 counterDeltaOk has no floor
confirmed.scenario: User removes a coin that was already deleted elsewhere (stale local list, multi-device) or double-taps the Remove pill (Detail.jsx:68 confirm, or Account PortRow:78) before the optimistic setPortfolio runs. Both calls succeed; the second is a no-op delete of a non-existent doc but STILL runs increment(coinCount, -1). The portfolio-update rule allows it (counterDeltaOk = ±1, no lower bound). Result: coinCount drops below the real coin count and can go negative.
confirmed.fixIdea: Guard removeCoin on the coin actually existing (read/transaction, or only decrement inside a transaction that confirms the doc was present) so a no-op delete doesn't decrement. Optionally clamp coinCount at 0 in the rule. Blast radius: a too-low/negative counter is a LIMIT OVERSHOOT — the user can hold more coins than their tier allows (a free user with coinCount=-1 can add 11 coins before maxCoins=10 blocks).

confirmed.title: No writer ever reconciles a drifted counter — seed/admin-SDK are consistent but nothing repairs drift, so every inflation/deflation is permanent
confirmed.where: functions/scripts/seed-emulator.js:37-49 (seed writes matching counters); functions/index.js:559-593 deleteUser/restoreUser (recursiveDelete whole tree, no surgical counter edits); firestore.rules relies on counters as the tier boundary
confirmed.scenario: The admin-SDK paths were checked as potential drift SOURCES and are clean: the seed sets portfolioCount=portfolios.length, each portfolio's coinCount to its real coin count, and txCount:0 with no tx (all consistent); deleteUser/purgeExpiredTrash recursiveDelete the entire user subtree (counters vanish with the docs, no drift); trash/restore only flip `deleted`. BUT there is NO server job, function, or client path that recomputes a counter from its real child-doc count. The counters are the security boundary that enforces plan limits, yet once Findings 1-4 corrupt one, it stays corrupted forever — an inflated coinCount permanently produces the reported false 'limit reached' toast, and a deflated one permanently allows limit overshoot.
confirmed.fixIdea: Add a reconciliation path: a small admin/callable (or a scheduled sweep) that recomputes coinCount = count(coins), txCount = count(transactions), portfolioCount = count(portfolios) and writes the true values via the Admin SDK. Even without fixing the writers, this bounds the blast radius and gives a recovery for accounts already stuck on the false limit.

confirmed.title: deletePortfolio decrements portfolioCount unconditionally — same double-decrement drift at the portfolio level
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-database.js:98-118 (deletePortfolio: batch.delete + increment(portfolioCount,-1), no existence guard); client guard only at CryptoIdea.jsx:466 (portfolios.length<=1); firestore.rules user-update L127 counterDeltaOk no floor
confirmed.scenario: A Pro/Premium user with >=2 portfolios double-taps delete on the same portfolio, or deletes a portfolio already removed on another device. The data layer has no existence guard and the client's `portfolios.length<=1` check reads pre-mutation state, so both calls pass. First delete removes the portfolio + portfolioCount-1; the second is a no-op delete but still runs increment(portfolioCount, -1). portfolioCount drifts below the real portfolio count (can go negative).
confirmed.fixIdea: Guard deletePortfolio on the portfolio existing before decrementing (read/transaction), mirroring the removeCoin fix. Blast radius: portfolioCount too low → portfolio-limit overshoot (create more portfolios than the tier permits).

confirmed.title: deleteTransaction decrements txCount unconditionally → txCount deflates on a stale/duplicate delete (tx-limit overshoot)
confirmed.where: src/api/firebase-database.js:325-336 (deleteTransaction: batch.delete + increment(txCount,-1), no existence guard); Detail.jsx:125 2-step delete confirm; coin-update rule L179 counterDeltaOk no floor
confirmed.scenario: User double-taps the tx "Delete?" confirm (Detail.jsx:125) or deletes a transaction already removed on another device. The second call is a no-op delete but still runs increment(txCount, -1), pushing txCount below the real transaction count (can go negative). addTransaction can't inflate (auto-generated doc id → a double-add creates two real docs and +2, which stays consistent), so txCount only drifts DOWN. Note the re-add path (Finding 1) also deflates a coin's txCount by resetting it to 0 via overwrite.
confirmed.fixIdea: Guard deleteTransaction on the tx existing before decrementing. Blast radius: txCount too low → transaction-limit overshoot (more tx per coin than the tier allows); combined with Finding 1's reset-to-0 it can badly under-count a busy coin.

confirmed.title: Downgrade 'trim' is pure client theater — server data is never deleted, everything resurrects on next login, and no server-side path trims either
confirmed.where: src/hooks/useUpgrade.js:108-112 (trimToTier = setPortfolios only); call sites src/CryptoIdea.jsx:677 (checkSubscriptionStatus), src/CryptoIdea.jsx:433 (declineProRecheckout), src/components/Login.jsx:108 (purchase completion / deferred Premium→Pro trim); resurrection via src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:28-41 (loadPortfolios reads full server state); no server trim: functions/index.js:1084-1096 + functions/billing.js:87-101 (subscriptionSweepPatch patches ONLY tier/subscription)
confirmed.scenario: Premium user with 3 portfolios / 15 coins cancels. Downgrade dialog explicitly warns '⚠ DATA THAT WILL BE DELETED … The following will be removed: • 2 portfolios • 5 coins' (CryptoIdea.jsx:823-832). After endDate, checkSubscriptionStatus → trimToTier('free') and the UI shows 1 portfolio / 10 coins. But trimToTier only calls setPortfolios — no dbRemoveCoin/dbDeletePortfolio/dbDeleteTransaction, and enforceSubscriptionPeriods only patches tier/subscription fields. The account then holds premium-scale data on the free tier forever: coinCount=15 > free cap 10 means firestore.rules (line 170-174) denies every new coin add — surfacing the exact founder-reported 'coin limit' toast via apiErrorMessage — while the existing over-cap data stays fully visible/editable (delete-only shrink; even after deleting down to 10 they still can't add, since getAfter=11 > 10). Users who deleted 5 coins themselves to 'make room' discover the app already claimed to have deleted them.

Simplest honest fix (KISS, matches existing rules): DON'T delete data on downgrade — remove trimToTier calls and rewrite the dialog to 'your data is kept but read-only above the new limits; new adds are blocked'. If deletion is the product intent, the trim must be real writes: batch dbDeleteTransaction/dbRemoveCoin/dbDeletePortfolio (which also keep coinCount/portfolioCount/txCount counters true), ideally server-side in the enforceSubscriptionPeriods sweep so it also covers users who never reopen the app.

confirmed.title: Trim keeps the WRONG survivors — dialog promises 'oldest removed, most recent kept' but the code keeps oldest portfolios, alphabetical coins, and OLDEST transactions (drops the newest)

Also fix the stale comment. Only worth doing as part of the finding-1 real-trim decision — if the product goes 'keep data, block adds', delete trimPortfolios instead.

The user, seeing 0 coins, re-adds e.g. bitcoin: the 'Already added' check passes, dbAddCoin's batch.set targets the EXISTING coins/bitcoin doc → Firestore treats it as an update → rules update branch allows it (validCoinData ok; txCount old≤1 → new 0 passes counterDeltaOk) and the parallel coinCount increment(1) passes counterDeltaOk('coinCount') with no cross-check → coinCount now exceeds the real doc count FOREVER (nothing heals counters; trimToTier is local-only per fact #5), so the user hits the coin cap early (e.g. blocked at 9 real coins on the free tier). The full-replace set also destroys the coin's journal (thesis data loss) and resets addedAt/txCount (txCount 1→0 desyncs the tx cap). Variant: if the existing coin has ≥2 transactions, counterDeltaOk('txCount') fails (0 >= 2-1 is false) → permission-denied → the same mislabeled 'coin limit' toast for a user who just tried to re-add a coin the UI lost.
confirmed.fixIdea: Make addCoin create-only: run it as a transaction that aborts if the coin doc exists (or getDoc-check first and surface a real 'already in this portfolio' message). Defense-in-depth in rules: on coin update require txCount to change by exactly 0 or -1 relative to resource.data (blocking the 0-reset shape addCoin sends), which also converts the corruption into a clean denial.

confirmed.title: watchCoins swallows mid-processing failures: a snapshot's changes are dropped PERMANENTLY (not 'last-good'), so a new coin can stay invisible on this device — feeding the re-add corruption

criticAdds.title: App Check is initialized but nothing handles its failure modes — at go-live (enforcement ON per the deploy checklist) a missing/blocked reCAPTCHA token turns EVERY Firestore write into permission-denied → the founder's limit toast app-wide, indistinguishable from a real limit
criticAdds.where: src/api/firebase.config.js:55-65 (initializeAppCheck only when !isDev && VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY; try/catch only console.warns; no user-facing signal); CLAUDE.md deploy-time checklist ('set VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY + enable App Check enforcement in console'); src/utils/errors.js:16-19 (permission-denied → limitMsg unconditionally); functions/guards.js appCheckOk (BL-1 — callables are gated, Firestore has no equivalent client-side awareness)
criticAdds.scenario: Two concrete go-live paths, neither mapped by any of the six dimensions: (1) enforcement is switched on in the console but the production build was made without VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY in env — initializeAppCheck never runs, every Firestore request from every user is rejected with permission-denied, and every addCoin shows "You've reached this portfolio's coin limit — upgrade for more" (a Starter user with 2 coins reproduces the founder's report exactly, at 100% rate, app-wide); (2) enforcement on and the key correct, but the user runs uBlock/Brave/a corporate proxy that blocks www.google.com/recaptcha — ReCaptchaV3Provider can't mint a token, all their Firestore traffic is denied, and only THAT user sees the limit toast on every action, unreproducible on the developer's machine. Because Firestore surfaces App Check rejections as the same 'permission-denied' code as a rules denial, apiErrorMessage can never label it honestly, and the init failure is only a console.warn. This is a third denial SOURCE (beyond rules-limit and rules-validity/eval) that the error-labeling mapper never enumerated.
criticAdds.fixIdea: Any fix for the mislabeled toast must stop treating permission-denied as 'limit' by inference; verify the limit server-side (e.g. re-read counters after a denial, or an addCoinGuarded callable that returns typed error codes). Additionally: surface App Check init failure to the UI, and smoke-test one Firestore read at startup to distinguish 'everything denied' (App Check/auth problem) from a per-write denial.

criticAdds.title: Offline is completely unhandled: no Firestore persistence, no timeout, no navigator.onLine — an offline addCoin hangs forever with zero feedback, and offline retaps queue duplicate commits that replay on reconnect into the empirically-confirmed coinCount-inflation bug
criticAdds.where: src/api/firebase.config.js:68 (plain getFirestore — no persistentLocalCache/enableIndexedDbPersistence anywhere; grep confirms); src/api/firebase-database.js:186 (addCoin awaits batch.commit(), which resolves only on server ack); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:493,499 (the 'Already added' guard and the optimistic append both run around that never-resolving await); grep: zero navigator.onLine / online-event handling in src/
criticAdds.scenario: A mobile PWA user loses connectivity (tunnel, elevator — the normal case for a phone portfolio app). They tap + Add: dbAddCoin's batch.commit() promise never resolves (memory-queued, no ack, no timeout), so there is no toast, no optimistic append, no spinner — Add silently does nothing. They tap Add again (and again): each tap passes the 'Already added' check (the local array was never updated) and enqueues ANOTHER batch targeting the SAME deterministic coin doc id. On reconnect the queue replays in order: commit #1 creates the coin (+1 coinCount), commits #2..n evaluate as UPDATEs under firestore.rules:179 (set on an existing doc, txCount 0 passes counterDeltaOk) and each still runs increment(coinCount,+1) — coinCount permanently inflated by n-1, which is the exact emulator-confirmed mechanism behind the founder's false 'coin limit' toast on later adds. Alternatively the user closes the tab while offline and the queued writes are silently lost (no persistence). The mappers confirmed the inflation mechanism but only via multi-device/double-tap races; the offline queue is the HIGH-probability real-world trigger and no finding mentions offline at all.
criticAdds.fixIdea: Disable the submit button while a write is in flight (kills the retap queue), add a write timeout (Promise.race ~10s → honest 'You appear to be offline' toast via navigator.onLine), and make addCoin create-safe server-side (rules: coin create must NOT match an existing doc / use a transaction that fails on exists) so replays can never inflate coinCount.

criticAdds.title: Suspension and trash don't actually stop writes: suspendUser only disables Auth (no token revocation, rules can't see 'disabled'), and firestore.rules never checks 'deleted' — a suspended user writes for up to ~1h, a trashed account can write its own tree indefinitely via the SDK
criticAdds.where: functions/index.js:543-556 (suspendUser: admin.auth().updateUser({disabled}) only — no revokeRefreshTokens, unlike the separate adminSignOutUser); firestore.rules:96-201 (every owner rule is isOwner+shape+counters; the 'deleted' flag is write-blocked for owners at rules:111,130 but READ by no rule); src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:67 (deleted gates only the client UI RestoreAccount screen)
criticAdds.scenario: (a) Admin suspends an abusive account (spam-registration bot, ToS violation). The target's current ID token stays valid up to ~1 hour and Firestore rules have no visibility of the Auth 'disabled' flag, so the account keeps creating portfolios/coins/transactions at full speed until token expiry — suspension appears to 'not work' during the incident that prompted it. (b) A user (or attacker with their creds) whose account is in the 30-day trash: signing in still works by design, the app shows RestoreAccount, but nothing stops direct SDK/REST writes — rules for coins/portfolios/tx check only isOwner + counters, never get(users/{uid}).data.deleted. A 'deleted' account can silently keep accumulating data (and its writes still count against/corrupt the counters that the limit system trusts). Neither gap produces the founder toast, but the suspended/trashed-writes dimension was explicitly in scope and no mapper covered it.
criticAdds.fixIdea: suspendUser should also revokeRefreshTokens(uid) (cuts the window to the ≤1h ID-token TTL, the platform minimum) — or mirror a 'suspended' flag onto users/{uid} and gate every owner write rule on !suspended && !deleted (one shared helper), which also closes the trashed-account write hole.

criticAdds.title: Admin Plans editor turns a cleared field into a hard 0 (''→0), mergePlans accepts 0 as a valid limit, and there is no way to express 'reset to default' — one accidental blank sets a tier's coin/portfolio/tx cap to 0 for every user on that tier, surfacing as limit-toast lockout app-wide
criticAdds.where: src/components/admin-dashboard.jsx:562-563 (onChange: e.target.value === "" ? 0 : Number(...) — min="0" allows it); functions/index.js:120-136 (mergePlans num() = x >= 0 accepts 0 and persists it; only non-numbers fall back to defaults); firestore.rules:71-81 (plan.get(key, fallback) returns the stored 0 → maxCoins 0); src/CryptoIdea.jsx:441-447 (_planLim's !=null keeps 0 too — BL-1e made 0 a respected value on purpose)
criticAdds.scenario: The solo admin edits Plans & Pricing, clears the free tier's 'coins' field intending to restore the default, and hits Save plans. The '' becomes 0, mergePlans validates 0 as legitimate, config/app.plans.free.coins = 0. From the next /api/config refresh (≤60s), every Starter user's maxCoinsPerPort is 0: the client pre-check blocks every add with 'Starter: 0 coins — upgrade to Pro for 50' (and if the config fetch hasn't landed yet, the server rules deny instead → the exact founder toast). Portfolio/tx fields fail identically ('Max 0 portfolios'). Because both layers agree, nothing looks like an error — the product is just silently capped at zero until the admin notices and re-types the numbers. There is no 'unset' affordance and no confirmation for a 0 limit. Admin-error-driven, but a one-keystroke, whole-tier, founder-symptom outage the config dimension mapping only covered in its malformed/eval-error variant, not this valid-0 variant.
criticAdds.fixIdea: In the plans editor, treat '' as 'unset' (omit the key so mergePlans falls back to the default) instead of 0, and require an explicit confirmation if an admin really types 0.
